name: Fixed income trend following
heading: The Structural Opportunity: Persistent Interest Rate Cycles
caseLead: Government bond yields can trend for several months as central banks adjust policy rates and investors revise expectations for growth and inflation. Economic data and policy guidance arrive over time, while changes in government borrowing and trade policy can sustain shifts in longer-term yield expectations.
caseRest: Unexpected inflation data or central bank guidance can reverse a bond yield trend and cause losses before positions are adjusted. The strategy then holds positions in the wrong direction and loses the gains of several weeks. It also earns little when yields move sideways, because trend signals reverse repeatedly and each trade incurs costs.
figNote: Each card shows the change in the US 10-year Treasury yield over the period described in the text, in basis points, where 100 basis points equal one percentage point. Bond trend following earns from sustained moves in yields in either direction, so a larger move offers more to follow.

events.title: Fed taper signal lifts Treasury yields
events.text: Between 2 May and 5 September 2013, the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 135bp after the Fed signalled that it would slow bond purchases. Results were mixed because the first rise reversed long positions at a loss, while the later trend rewarded short positions.

events.title: Tariff escalation drives a bond rally
events.text: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 55bp between July and late August 2019 as higher US tariffs on Chinese goods raised growth concerns. The strategy gained because it held long bond positions while yields fell steadily.

events.title: Covid sends yields to record lows then reverses
events.text: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 130bp from mid-January to 9 March 2020 as Covid spread, then rose about 65bp in nine days as investors sold Treasuries for cash. Results were mixed because long bond positions gained in the fall but lost in the reversal.

events.title: Fed tightening starts the steepest bond sell-off
events.text: Between January and October 2022, the 10-year Treasury yield rose about 260bp as the Fed raised rates to control inflation. The strategy gained because short bond positions rewarded the steady rise in yields.

events.title: Silicon Valley Bank failure reverses bond trends
events.text: The 10-year Treasury yield fell about 50bp between 8 and 15 March 2023 after the failure of Silicon Valley Bank, as investors expected the Fed to pause. The strategy lost because short positions built during the earlier rise in yields reversed within days.

events.title: US tariffs lift Treasury yields sharply
events.text: The 10-year Treasury yield rose about 48bp in the week to 11 April 2025, the largest weekly rise since 2001, as US tariffs unsettled bond investors. The strategy lost because long positions built during the earlier decline in yields reversed within days.

instrument: Government bond futures in the US, Germany, UK, Japan, Canada and Australia; held for weeks; rolled quarterly
rules: Long when the 1-month and 6-month yield trends both fall, short when both rise; positions reduced when rate volatility rises; contracts rolled before first notice
costs: Estimated commissions, bid-ask spreads and futures roll costs deducted at each trade
constructionTitle: Strategy construction, from yield trends to duration-balanced risk

legs.position: Long or short US Treasury futures
Long or short German and UK bond futures
Long or short Japanese and Canadian bond futures
legs.purpose: Earns trends in other major markets

legs.position: Long or short Australian bond futures

entry: 1-month and 6-month yield trends agree in direction
size: Set to a 7% annualised volatility target, with each market at most 25% of risk
exit: Position closed when the 1-month trend turns against the 6-month trend
stop: Market position closed after a loss of 1.5% of portfolio value
marketWatch: Rehyn watches the direction of policy rate expectations in the major economies and the pace of change in inflation, because these set the length of yield trends. Rising interest rate volatility suggests a higher risk of reversal. Central bank meetings, inflation releases and government borrowing announcements are the events most likely to start or end a trend.

favourable.heading: Clear central bank rate cycles
favourable.text: Rate cycles that central banks signal in advance favour the strategy because yields keep moving in one direction for many months. In 2022, successive Fed rate rises lifted the 10-year Treasury yield by about 260bp, and the strategy gained from short positions.

favourable.heading: Flight to safety in slowdowns
favourable.text: Slowing growth favours the strategy because investors buy government bonds and yields fall in a steady trend. During the 2019 trade war, the 10-year Treasury yield fell about 55bp, and long positions gained.

favourable.heading: Persistent inflation or heavy borrowing
favourable.text: Persistent inflation or heavier government borrowing favours the strategy because yields rise over several quarters as investors ask for higher compensation. The UK 10-year gilt yield rose from about 1% at the end of 2021 to above 4.5% in 2023.

adverse.heading: Policy pivots after long trends
adverse.text: A sudden shift in central bank guidance hurts the strategy when it reverses a trend that has lasted for months. In March 2023, the failure of Silicon Valley Bank cut the 10-year Treasury yield by about 50bp in a week and reversed short positions.

adverse.heading: Forced selling that reverses trends
adverse.text: Forced selling of government bonds hurts the strategy when it reverses long positions within days. In mid-March 2020, the 10-year yield rose about 65bp in nine days as investors sold Treasuries to raise cash, after a fall of about 130bp.

adverse.heading: Range-bound yields without direction
adverse.text: Periods when yields move sideways hurt the strategy because trend signals reverse repeatedly and trading costs accumulate. In 2017, the 10-year Treasury yield stayed between about 2.0% and 2.6% for the full year.

infoHist: Historical results show the strategy's peak-to-trough drawdown during each event, measured from its value just before the event to its lowest point using the default backtest parameters above. Each event window runs from the last market high before the shock to the market low.
infoForward: Scenario results show the estimated profit or loss over the first month of each scenario. Rehyn's scenario engine projects moves in government bond yields in each market, which are then applied to the strategy's current positions.
